editorial: We went in early September, just as the summer (June to August) was transitioning into fall (September and October). We were fortunate enough to see the aurora on two of the four nights we stayed, but it’s far from a guarantee at this time of the year.

There is no single perfect time for Iceland, which makes it a choose-your-own adventure. If you want to experience the midnight sun, then summer is the time for you. If you insist on witnessing the northern lights, then the winter (November to March) is your best bet, but beware the biting cold.
If you’re like us and just want to see spectacular landscapes and have enough daylight to drive around, then spring (April and May) and fall work splendidly.
